title: Picking a layer stops re-measuring the whole right hand panel
goal: When you click a layer, the right hand panel works out its whole height again from scratch, because the click changes which sections it shows. On a small document that is the single slowest thing about the click: the app spends about twenty milliseconds in one go re-measuring the panel, which is more than a frame, and it happens on every pick that brings a section in or takes one away.
notes:
Split out of picking-a-layer-lands-within-a-frame-in-a-long-l on 2026-09-15, which finished the LIST half and measured this as what is left.

MeASURED (locked screen, PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1, so the absolute numbers are understated but the comparison is same-run):
  two rows, pick swaps [layers] <-> [layers, geometry]: mainBusy 20-36ms, LONGEST SINGLE PASS 14-25ms, inspectorPanel bodies 1-2
  eighteen rows, pick keeps the same sections [layers,color,effects,motion]: mainBusy 11-12ms, longest pass 7.6-8.6ms, inspectorPanel bodies 1
So it is not list length and it is not the number of sections drawn, it is the ARRIVAL: a section coming in or going out makes the dock share its height out again. The mechanisms are PanelSectionArrival and DockArrivals (Sources/Photonz/InspectorPanel.swift, the arrivalPass counter), DockBudgetScratch (a struct in @State, so every height a section measures rebuilds the panel) and InspectorDockLayout. The earlier task already cut the four passes per pick down to two by refusing to record a departing section's last measurement; what is left is the two that remain and what each of them re-measures.

The walk to use is Scripts/playtest/layer-pick-latency-walk.json: its selectRow steps report mainBusy, longest pass and the per-view body counts, and InspectorPanel logs one trace line per dock pass saying which sections and what budget it drew at.
acceptance: No single pass of main thread work in a pick runs past one frame at sixty hertz, on a two row document as well as a long one, measured by Scripts/playtest/layer-pick-latency-walk.json
A pick that changes which sections the panel shows costs no more main thread work than one that does not
The panel still builds at most twice per pick and nothing outside it builds at all
Sections still arrive and leave without anything under them jumping

log.note: Adversarial review of the task BEFORE building: the goal says the panel 'works out its whole height again from scratch' and that this is the twenty milliseconds. I could not take that on trust, so I measured it by ablation before changing anything. It is not true. Reproduced the baseline first (layer-pick-latency-walk, screen locked so PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1, comparisons same-session): selectRow 22-42ms busy / 13-30ms longest, selectCanvas 50-71 / 27-39.

Built a steadier benchmark than the walk: a blank 900x700 canvas with a rectangle and an arrow on it, picked alternately twenty times, medians over 38 picks. Baseline 46.4ms busy / 28.6ms longest single pass. Then took one piece out at a time: dock hidden 12.9/9.8; every section body blanked 16.6/13.4; layers list back, forms blank 22.6/19.4; everything back 46.4/28.6. So a pick is ~10ms canvas and selection, ~4ms dock shell, ~6ms the layers list drawing itself again, ~10ms building the arriving section's form.

Everything this task names costs nothing measurable. Per-section chrome removed (tutorial anchor, frame reader, lift, offsets, animation, drop target): 44.6/28.8, no change. .regularMaterial removed: 46.6/29.0, no change. DockBudgetScratch's @State writes: no-ops once a section's height has been seen once, which after the first pick is always, so bodies stay at 2 per pick. PanelSectionArrival EARNS its keep: turning the deferral off put the longest pass UP, 29.7 to 33.3ms. Replacing the ScrollView made it worse still, 38.0. Stubbing the probe-only PanelTarget and HelpAnchor NSViews changed nothing, so these numbers are honest about the shipping build and not an artefact of the harness.

What it IS: making AppKit controls. Two TextFields in the Canvas section are 6ms on their own, the colour well 2ms, so roughly 3-5ms per control with no single villain. A section coming in builds its whole form from nothing because a view taken out of a ForEach loses its identity, and no bookkeeping in InspectorPanel can make that cheaper. Acceptance 1 is also unreachable through this panel either way: with the dock hidden altogether a pick is still 9.8ms in its longest pass, and the layers list is 6ms on three rows.

Shipped the measurement rather than a change: commit e43154ad puts the whole breakdown and the method in a comment above `arrivals` in Sources/Photonz/InspectorPanel.swift, next to the machinery three tasks in a row have now suspected. Scripts/test.sh green (7668 tests); layer-pick-latency-walk and layer-pick-at-scale-walk both pass. Filed a-section-that-appears-in-the-right-hand-panel-a to carry the user-facing goal with the right target and the reproduction.

left rough: the layers list rebuilds twice per pick (layersList bodies 2), once for the click and once for the arrival pass, at ~3ms each on a three row list. Making it skip the parent-driven one would need .equatable(), which LibraryPanel's own comment warns against for exactly this panel, and ~3ms of 28.6 does not pay for that risk. Noted here rather than filed.

Measured by ablation before building: the dock's height budget, the arrival bookkeeping and the per-section chrome this task names cost nothing. A pick's panel cost is building the arriving section's form out of AppKit controls, ~3-5ms each, which no bookkeeping in InspectorPanel can reach. The measurement is committed (e43154ad) next to the machinery, and a-section-that-appears-in-the-right-hand-panel-a carries the user-facing goal with the right target.
